title: Error E-42
scenario: A router company runs a support bot. It searches the knowledge base with embeddings only, takes the top 5 chunks and passes them to the model. A customer reports an error code, and the bot answers with general advice instead of the fix. You review the retrieval trace (exhibit).
exhibit:
RETRIEVAL TRACE
query:  My X200 shows error E-42 after the update
search: embeddings only, top 5

#  score  source
1  0.62   kb://error-codes-overview
2  0.60   kb://x200-firmware-update-guide
3  0.58   kb://x200-faq
4  0.57   kb://x100-error-list
5  0.55   kb://warranty-terms

NOT RETRIEVED
kb://x200-error-e42
  E-42: firmware checksum failed. Hold RESET
  for 10 seconds, then reinstall the update.

questions.prompt: Why did search miss the chunk about E-42?

options.text: The E-42 chunk is too short, so embedding models skip it.
options.explanation: Short chunks still get a vector. The issue is what the vector captures: general meaning, not the exact code.

options.text: Embeddings matched the general topic but missed the exact code.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's TS-999 example: an embedding model may find content about error codes in general but miss the exact match.

options.text: The query mixes a model name and an error code in one sentence.
options.explanation: That is a normal support question. Keyword search would match both terms; embeddings alone blur them.

options.text: The vector store is out of date because the update is new.
options.explanation: The E-42 chunk is in the store, listed under NOT RETRIEVED. It exists but ranks too low.

questions.prompt: The team uses the OpenAI Retrieval API. Which change gives exact words like E-42 more weight?

options.text: Set `rewrite_query=true` so OpenAI rewrites the question.
options.explanation: Query rewriting tidies a chatty question into a search string. It does not change how keyword and meaning matches are balanced.

options.text: Raise `score_threshold` to 0.9 to keep only strong matches.
options.explanation: A threshold only removes low-scoring chunks. The E-42 chunk already scores too low, so it would still be missing.

options.text: Set `max_num_results` to 50 so more chunks come back.
options.explanation: More results might include it by luck, but they also add tokens and noise. The ranking itself still ignores the exact code.
Right. OpenAI says a higher `text_weight` emphasizes textual overlap in the reciprocal rank fusion.

questions.prompt: Hybrid search now returns 150 candidates. The team wants to send the model only the best 20. What does Anthropic's post do?

options.text: Score the 150 with a reranking model and keep the top 20.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic retrieved the top 150, reranked them against the query and passed the top 20 to the model.

options.text: Send all 150 chunks, since more context always helps.
options.explanation: Anthropic warns that more information can be distracting for models. Reranking also reduces cost and latency.

options.text: Keep the 20 chunks with the shortest text to save tokens.
options.explanation: Length says nothing about relevance. The short chunks could all be off-topic.

options.text: Keep the first 20 in the order the database returned them.
options.explanation: That is the rough first ranking the team wants to improve. A reranker re-scores each chunk against the query.

questions.prompt: The bot runs on Claude. The team wants every answer to cite the article it used. What should they send?

options.text: The chunks as plain text, with an instruction to add links at the end.
options.explanation: Then the model writes links as free text, which nothing checks. Search result blocks give structured citations instead.

options.text: A list of all article URLs in the system prompt, before the chunks.
options.explanation: A list of URLs does not tie any sentence to its source. Citations need the content and its source together.

options.text: Each chunk as a `search_result` block, with citations enabled.
options.explanation: Right. Each block carries a `source` such as `kb://x200-error-e42`, a title and the text, and Claude cites them.

options.text: Only the top chunk, so the answer can only come from one place.
options.explanation: That still gives no citation the user can see, and it drops other chunks that may be needed.
